paras: The Macon quarantine shooting took place at noon on Thursday, August 3, 1905, in Macon, Noxubee County, Mississippi, when two men, Sam Irion and a Mr. Maury, fired their pistols at a Black man who had left a railroad car without a health certificate. The man fired back, escaped across a cornfield, and was not found by the sheriff's bloodhounds; the only known report, in the local Macon Beacon, treated it as "An Exciting Incident."

In early August 1905 Macon had put a yellow-fever quarantine on towns below Meridian after a case was reported at Lumberton, and guards were appointed to meet the trains. The same issue of the Beacon complained that Black workers were "rush[ing] back" from the infected counties and that some had arrived with health certificates "purchased" at the Meridian depot.

According to the Beacon, the man started down the steps of a car and was told by Irion that he could not get off without the proper certificate. The paper said he answered "in an insolent manner," jumped off and ran, and that a shot fired "to frighten him" only made him run faster. Irion kept firing, and as the man passed Scales' warehouse Maury also "opened up on him."

The man then stopped, took cover behind a post and fired back, and by the time both men had emptied their pistols he had got away across the cornfield west of the oil mill. No one is reported wounded on either side.

Sheriff Dantzler sent for the county's bloodhounds, but they arrived three hours later and failed to follow the trail. The coverage does not show whether the man was later caught or whether anyone was charged over the shooting.

The incident appears only as a short local item on the second page of the Macon Beacon of August 5, beside the paper's long report on the quarantine. The item names the shooters as "Mr." Irion and "Mr." Maury, calls the target only "the negro," and explains the gunfire through his "insolent" reply and his flight. Its tone is light, describing the man as proceeding "to do some shooting himself" and closing on the bloodhounds' failure.
No other white paper and no Black paper carrying the story was found.

bases: Two named men, apparently enforcing the town's quarantine-certificate rule, fired repeatedly on a fleeing Black man who fired back and escaped, after which the sheriff tried to track him with bloodhounds (A2, A1); there was no crowd and no one is reported hurt.
The incident appears in only one report, the local Macon Beacon (A2); no other white paper and no Black paper carrying it was found.

accounts.label: Local paper (shooters' side)
accounts.gist: The man answered insolently, jumped off and ran; a first shot was fired only to frighten him, and he later fired back from behind a post before escaping.

framing.detail: The Macon Beacon's "An Exciting Incident" presents the shooting as a lively local item, stresses the man's "insolent manner" and the warning shot, and closes on the failure of the bloodhounds.
